Hi! My name is **Jiahao Tian**. I am an undergraduate student majoring
in Statistics at the
[School of Mathematical Sciences](http://www.math.zju.edu.cn),
**Zhejiang University**.

My research interests lie at the intersection of **high-dimensional
inference**, **uncertainty quantification**, and **theoretical
statistics**. I am particularly interested in developing statistically
principled methods that remain reliable under distribution shift,
heavy-tailed distributions, and other forms of model misspecification.

I am currently working on conformal prediction under covariate shift
and robust multiple-knockoff aggregation.

## Research Interests

- High-Dimensional Statistical Inference
- Multiple Testing and False Discovery Rate Control
- Conformal Prediction and Uncertainty Quantification
- Distribution Shift and Robust Statistics

## Research

### Heavy-Tailed Robustness of Multiple-Knockoff Aggregation Methods

**Advisor:** [Prof. Lijun Wang](https://hohoweiya.xyz/), Zhejiang University  
*September 2025–Present*

I study the robustness of multiple-knockoff aggregation procedures under
heavy-tailed distributions, with particular attention to selection
instability, signal dilution, and threshold inflation.

[More about this project →](Projects/index.qmd)

### Distributional Balancing Weights for Conformal Calibration under Covariate Shift

**Advisor:** [Prof. Guanhua Chen](https://sites.google.com/view/gchenwisc/),
UW–Madison  
*March 2026–Present*

I develop distributional balancing methods for conformal prediction
under covariate shift, using tools from Fourier analysis, RKHS theory,
and empirical process theory.

[More about this project →](Projects/index.qmd)
